CurrentRulesContent:
Game flow

  • There are four players. At the start of a round, each player draws a numbered card; the highest card starts. Ties are redrawn.
  • Play a card matching the current color or value. Wild cards can be played regardless of color.
  • If no playable card exists, draw one card. When Draw Until Playable is enabled, keep drawing until a playable card is found. A playable drawn card can be played or kept.
  • If the deck is empty and the player cannot play, that player is knocked out.

Player statuses

  • Normal: no temporary status.
  • UNO: the player has called UNO while holding two cards and is ready to play down to one card. The UNO button disappears after a successful call.
  • +N: the player must draw N penalty cards.
  • *N: in Death Match, the player will lose N percent of maximum HP at the next turn because the hand is above the threshold.
  • KnockOut: HP reached zero, or the deck ran out while the player had no playable card. The player skips the rest of the game.

UNO

  • When the human player has exactly two cards and at least one playable card, the UNO button is shown.
  • Call UNO before playing the card that leaves one card in hand. If UNO was not called, the player draws the configured UNO penalty, from 1 to 4 cards; the default is 2.
  • The UNO status lasts until the player's turn ends. AI players call UNO automatically when required.

Penalties and stacking

  • Skip makes the next player lose the turn.
  • Draw Two and Wild Draw Four give the next player a draw penalty. Same-type stacking can be enabled independently.
  • Cross-type Draw Two and Draw Four stacking is available when the cross-type option is enabled.
  • When penalty transfer is enabled, a matching Skip or Reverse can pass the penalty onward or send it back according to the play direction.
  • If the penalty cannot be avoided or stacked, the player draws the accumulated penalty and the penalty state is cleared.

Game modes

  • Traditional: the round ends when any player empties their hand. The player with the lowest remaining-card point total wins.
  • Battle Puno: the round ends when any player empties their hand. Every player's HP is reduced by the point total of their remaining cards, and remaining HP is added to score. The game ends when a player reaches the score goal.
  • Death Match: uses Battle Puno scoring. At the start of a turn, a hand below the initial hand size is replenished. A hand above initial size plus one increases the escalating *N damage status. The game ends when the human player is knocked out, only one player remains, or the score goal is reached.

Special cards

  • Zero: in Battle Puno and Death Match, choose +10 damage or reset the damage pool. It has no damage-pool choice in Traditional.
  • Reverse: reverses play direction and can transfer a penalty.
  • Wild: choose the next color.
  • Wild Chaos: randomly chooses the next color and value.
  • Trade: exchange the complete hand with another player.
  • Wild Hit All: every other active player draws two cards; this draw cannot be avoided.
  • Discard All: discard every card matching the current color.
  • Trade, Wild Chaos, Wild Hit All, and Discard All are available only when extra cards are enabled; Trade also has its own setting.

Current setting limits

  • Initial hand: 4 to 10 cards, default 7.
  • Initial HP: 50 to 1000, default 200.
  • Score goal: 100 to 5000, default 500.
  • UNO penalty: 1 to 4 cards, default 2.
  • Deck size: 0 means an inexhaustible deck; a custom deck must contain at least 100 cards.
BasicContent:
(the rules will be different from the offiical uno rules)

The Basic Game Flow:

Beginning:
At the beginning of the game, each player draws a card from the deck, and the player with the highest card point(see the 'Card Point' below) will play first with clockwise order. The card drawn will be visible for about 2 seconds.
Then, a first card will be drawn from the deck, which indicates the next card should be played.



Main process:
The one plays the card must play the card matched to last card's colour(red/blue/green/yellow) or symbol(0-9, skip, reverse......). The wild cards can be played regardless of the color of previous card. The player will have to draw a card from the deck if he/she has no matched card to play(or simply doesn't want to play). When any player has no cards in the hand, the round ends and calculate the score.


Hint: Click on the deck to draw a card, click on the card to play it, if it doesn't match, it won't be played.


Overtime:
When it comes there's no card left on deck, the game continues. If the player has no more card to play, he/she keeps the card in hand but no longer be able to play in this round(knocked out). The rest players follow the same process until there's only one player left and he/she also has no card to play.
TraditionalContent: The traditional UNO mode, the goal is simple: empty the hand cards. But when you facing the penalty draws, you can play the skip/reverse card corresponding to its color to avoid the penalty by passing it to next player(skip) or counter to last player(reverse).
BattlePunoContent:
In this mode, when a player played all of his/her hand cards. The round ends and everyone's hp will be reduced by the sum of card points in the hand, then the hitpoints left will convert to score.
The game ends whenever a player reachs the score goal.



Taking damage and calculating:
When a numbered card is played, the damage pool will increased by its number. And if a player draws from the deck without penalty, he/she will take all damage in the damage pool, then the pool will reset to 0.

the damage effect is based on the cards in damage pool.
DeathMatchContent:
To be the last stand to win the game. Besides the rules from 'Battle Puno!', player will have to draw the card until the hand has same number as initially has. if player holding 2 more cards than initially has, from next of his/her turn, no matter skipped, will loses 1% of max hp, and 2%, 3%...and so on until having less than the 'threshold'. The status will shows as '*1', '*2'...representing the hp percentage will be lost next turn.
Also, a 'stacking penalty draw' will be applied. Player can also avoid the penalty draw by play any penalty draw card in the hand, but will draws will increased.


as the screenshot shows, '+10' is the result of stacked penalty and *3 means will loses hp equivalent to 3% of max hp next turn. And the damage effect is based on the cards the player has.
